surfaceForm: becomes a self-service capability for the institution's consumers ... the institution stops thinking about "the playbook" and starts thinking about routine operations
location: ch27-wave9-lifecycle-EN.tex, opening paragraph (after \chapter, before \section{Goal and dependencies})
proposedGenericDecision: "the institution" is already a role-based placeholder for the adopting organisation; this usage is institution-agnostic and should be retained as the canonical generic actor term.
rationale: The text uses "the institution" as a generic role, not as University of Luxembourg. Flagging only to confirm the term is the intended agnostic actor; no change required.

surfaceForm: self-service is rolled out per consumer group, not institution-wide ... rolled out group by group rather than institution-wide
proposedGenericDecision: Assumes a single bounded "institution" whose perimeter defines the rollout scope. For a multi-tenant / federated adopter (e.g. a university group, a ministry covering several establishments) the unit of rollout is the adopting-organisation perimeter. Reword the boundary as "organisation-wide" or "adopter-wide".
rationale: "institution-wide" presumes a single-institution governance perimeter. Generic framing should let the adopter define its own outer boundary without assuming one campus / one legal entity.

surfaceForm: a research group with mature DevOps practice first, then teaching environments where the requester is the instructor, then administrative services where the requester is typically a unit manager
proposedGenericDecision: The research / teaching / administrative consumer triad and the "instructor" / "unit manager" requester roles assume a specific university org chart. Keep as an illustrative example but mark it explicitly as indicative role labels the adopter maps to its own structure.
rationale: Role names (instructor, unit manager) and the three-consumer-group taxonomy are university-shaped. They are illustrative rather than UL-specific, so soften to indicative rather than parameterize.

surfaceForm: a faculty-level service-management heterogeneity ... does not eliminate faculty-level autonomy in service management ... faculty-specific extensions build on ... respects faculty autonomy
proposedGenericDecision: "faculty" encodes a specific university sub-unit structure. Replace with a role-based term such as "autonomous sub-unit" / "organisational division" so the pattern fits any federated adopter (faculties, departments, agencies, member institutions).
rationale: Repeated reliance on "faculty" assumes a university-style sub-unit. A localization variable lets non-university or differently-structured adopters substitute their own division term while preserving the autonomy-vs-baseline argument.

surfaceForm: demonstrated stability for an institutionally agreed period (indicatively three to six months)
proposedGenericDecision: Concrete duration constants are presented as defaults. They are already hedged as "institutionally agreed" and "indicative", which is the desired generic form; retain the hedge, keep the indicative figure as a non-binding example.
rationale: Durations are explicitly framed as indicative and adopter-agreed, so they do not bind a specific institution. Flagged for completeness; no change needed beyond confirming the hedge stays.

surfaceForm: Indicative duration is four to six months for the technical configuration
proposedGenericDecision: Same as other indicative durations: already hedged as "indicative". Retain as a non-binding default; ensure it is not read as a UL-calibrated figure.
rationale: Hedged indicative figure, adopter-tunable. No institution-binding; flagged for completeness.

surfaceForm: Indicative duration. Twelve to twenty-four months (appears twice: brownfield MS and brownfield hybrid)
location: ch27-wave9-lifecycle-EN.tex, §Trajectory: brownfield Microsoft-centric (sec:w9-brownfield-ms) and §Trajectory: brownfield hybrid (sec:w9-brownfield-hybrid)
proposedGenericDecision: Indicative duration constants, already hedged. Retain as non-binding examples; no institution-specific calibration implied.
rationale: Hedged indicative figures applicable to any adopter; not UL-bound.

surfaceForm: built around ServiceNow, Microsoft Service Management, or a comparable ITSM platform ... Trajectory: brownfield Microsoft-centric
proposedGenericDecision: Named commercial products (ServiceNow, Microsoft Service Management) and "Microsoft-centric" section title are vendor-specific but used as representative ITSM exemplars, not as a UL deployment claim. The phrase "or a comparable ITSM platform" already generalises. Keep named exemplars as illustrations of a vendor-class; they are not institution identity, so retain.
rationale: These are third-party product names used as generic-class exemplars, not markers of University of Luxembourg. They make the brownfield trajectory concrete for any adopter and are already softened with "or a comparable ITSM platform". Not an institution-agnostic blocker.

surfaceForm: SLSA / Sigstore attestations ... NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d) ... EU AI Act, Art. 53 ... 27001 A.8.30 ... NIST CSF GOVERN (GV.SC) / IDENTIFY (ID.AM) ... COBIT APO10 / BAI03
proposedGenericDecision: These are external standards/regulations and tooling (EU instruments, ISO, NIST, COBIT, SLSA, Sigstore), not UL-specific identifiers. They are deliberately generic normative anchors and must be retained. The only latent jurisdiction assumption is reliance on EU instruments (NIS2, EU AI Act) without naming the jurisdiction.
rationale: Framework/regulation citations are jurisdiction-level (EU) normative anchors common to the whole suite, not institution-identifying. Retain; jurisdiction-scoping is handled at suite level (see separate EU-assumption row).

surfaceForm: Under the EU AI Act, Art. 53 ... It is the principal anchor of NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d) ... contributes to NIST CSF GOVERN
proposedGenericDecision: The chapter silently assumes the adopter is subject to EU regulatory instruments (NIS2, EU AI Act) without naming the jurisdiction. For a non-EU adopter the supply-chain/lifecycle anchor would map to local equivalents. Parameterize the binding-jurisdiction so the regulatory anchor set is adopter-selected, or add a guard that EU instruments are the worked example.
suggestedLocalizationVariable: REGULATORY_REGIME (default: EU = NIS2 + EU AI Act; adopter substitutes local supply-chain / AI-governance instruments)
rationale: EU instruments are stated as the operative regime without naming the country/jurisdiction. This is an implicit national-transposition assumption: the lifecycle-loop anchor is regime-bound and should be parameterizable for non-EU adopters while EU stays the documented default.

surfaceForm: typically those participating in NSF ACCESS or EGI federations ... reported in NREN community fora and in EDUCAUSE publications
proposedGenericDecision: NSF ACCESS (US), EGI (EU), NREN fora and EDUCAUSE are region-specific research-infrastructure programs/bodies used as illustrative precedents. They assume a US/EU research-computing context. Keep as cited examples but optionally mark as region-representative so adopters in other regions read them as exemplars, not requirements.
rationale: These named federations/bodies are sector precedents (evidence Layer 5/3), not UL identity. They carry an implicit US/EU regional assumption; softening to "region-specific examples" preserves the evidence while removing the geographic presumption.

surfaceForm: the international peer comparison anticipated in phase 2 begins to operate against the institution's longitudinal record
proposedGenericDecision: "phase 2" references an external roadmap/phasing defined elsewhere in the suite. If that phasing is UL-program-specific it leaks an institution-specific plan; if it is a generic suite construct it is fine. Verify against the suite roadmap and either keep (generic) or generalize the phase label.
rationale: "phase 2" appears to be an internal suite-roadmap construct rather than a UL identifier, but it presumes a defined two-phase program. Flag for cross-check against the suite roadmap; no UL string present, so default to keep pending verification.
